7	---
8	
9	### Cosets and the coset space `G/H`
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	For a subgroup `H` of a group `𝑮`, we say that two elements, `x, y` in `𝑮`, lie in the same
14	**left coset**, and we write `x ∼ y`, exactly when `x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H`.
15	
16	In the setoid discipline the coset space `G / H` is not a new carrier of
17	equivalence classes but the *same* carrier with a coarser setoid equality: the
18	relation `_∼_` just described.
19	
20	This module proves `_∼_` is an equivalence relation and packages the quotient
21	setoid, `cosetSetoid`{.AgdaFunction}, via the `_/_`{.AgdaFunction} construction of
22	[Setoid.Relations.Quotients][].
23	
24	Two further lemmas prepare the ground for the coset action of
25	[Classical.Structures.Group.GSet][]: the original setoid equality refines the
26	coset equality (`≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction}, well-definedness of the quotient map), and
27	left translation by any group element preserves the coset equality
28	(`∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, which will be the congruence proof of the action).
29	
30	<!--
31	```agda
32	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
33	
34	module Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets where
35	
36	open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )
37	
38	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------
39	open import Data.Product     using ( _,_ ; proj₁ )
40	open import Level            using ( Level )
41	open import Relation.Binary  using ( Setoid ; IsEquivalence )
42	open import Relation.Nullary using ( Dec )
43	open import Relation.Unary   using ( Pred ; _∈_ )
44	
45	import Algebra.Properties.Group as GroupProperties
46	import Relation.Binary.Reasoning.Setoid as SetoidReasoning
47	
48	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------
49	open import Overture                              using ( Equivalence )
50	open import Classical.Bundles.Group               using ( ⟨_⟩ᵍᵖ )
51	open import Classical.Structures.Group.Basic      using ( Group ; module Group-Op )
52	open import Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups  using ( IsSubgroup )
53	open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic                 using ( Algebra ; 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] )
54	open import Setoid.Relations.Quotients            using ( _/_ )
55	```
56	-->
57	
58	#### The coset relation
59	
60	```agda
61	module Coset {α ρ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) {ℓ : Level}
62	  (H : Pred 𝕌[ proj₁ 𝒢 ] ℓ) (H-isSubgroup : IsSubgroup 𝒢 H)
63	  where
64	
65	  private
66	    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
67	    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
68	
69	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]            using ( _≈_ )
70	                                renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
71	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
72	  open Group-Op 𝒢               using  ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
73	                                       ; assoc-law ; invˡ-law )
74	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ  using  ( ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙
75	                                       ; \\-leftDividesˡ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
76	  open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup  using  ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed ; ⁻¹-closed )
77	
78	  infix 4 _∼_
79	
80	  -- x and y lie in the same left coset of H when x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H.
81	  _∼_ : G → G → Type ℓ
82	  x ∼ y = x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H
83	```
84	
85	#### `_∼_` is an equivalence relation
86	
87	+  Reflexivity is `ε ∈ H` transported along `x ⁻¹ ∙ x ≈ ε`.
88	+  Symmetry is closure of `H` under inverses, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x`.
89	+  Transitivity is closure under products, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z`.
90	
91	```agda
92	  ∼-refl : ∀ {x} → x ∼ x
93	  ∼-refl {x} = respects (≈sym (invˡ-law x)) ε-closed
94	
95	  ∼-sym : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → y ∼ x
96	  ∼-sym {x} {y} x∼y = respects inv-eq (⁻¹-closed x∼y)
97	    where
98	    inv-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x
99	    inv-eq = begin
100	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (x ⁻¹) y ⟩
101	      y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-involutive x) ⟩
102	      y ⁻¹ ∙ x          ∎
103	
104	  ∼-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x ∼ y → y ∼ z → x ∼ z
105	  ∼-trans {x} {y} {z} x∼y y∼z = respects prod-eq (∙-closed x∼y y∼z)
106	    where
107	    prod-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z
108	    prod-eq = begin
109	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z)  ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) y (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ⟩
110	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (y ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesˡ y z) ⟩
111	      x ⁻¹ ∙ z                 ∎
112	
113	  ∼-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _∼_
114	  ∼-isEquivalence = record { refl = ∼-refl ; sym = ∼-sym ; trans = ∼-trans }
115	
116	  ∼-equivalence : Equivalence G {ℓ}
117	  ∼-equivalence = _∼_ , ∼-isEquivalence
118	```
119	
120	#### Compatibility lemmas
121	
122	Two facts are needed before the coset relation can be used as an equality.
123	
124	`≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} says the group's own setoid equality refines the coset
125	relation, which is what makes the quotient map well defined: equal elements land
126	in the same coset.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} says left translation by any group
127	element preserves the coset relation, which is what lets `g ∙_` descend to the
128	coset space.
129	
130	Both are proved the same way, by supplying `respects`{.AgdaFunction} with an
131	equality between the relevant `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` witnesses: for `≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} that
132	witness reduces to `ε` and membership follows from `ε-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, and for
133	`∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} the `g` cancels, so the translated witness equals the
134	original.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} is what
135	[Classical.Structures.Group.GSet][] uses to build the coset algebra.
136	
137	```agda
138	  -- The setoid equality refines the coset equality (the quotient map is well defined).
139	  ≈⇒∼ : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∼ y
140	  ≈⇒∼ {x} {y} x≈y = respects (≈sym unit-eq) ε-closed
141	    where
142	    unit-eq : x ⁻¹ ∙ y ≈ ε
143	    unit-eq = ≈trans (∙-cong (⁻¹-cong x≈y) ≈refl) (invˡ-law y)
144	
145	  -- Left translation by any group element preserves the coset equality.
146	  ∼-congˡ : ∀ g {x y} → x ∼ y → (g ∙ x) ∼ (g ∙ y)
147	  ∼-congˡ g {x} {y} x∼y = respects (≈sym transl-eq) x∼y
148	    where
149	    transl-eq : (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ y
150	    transl-eq = begin
151	      (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)     ≈⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ≈refl ⟩
152	      x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)    ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) (g ∙ y) ⟩
153	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g y) ⟩
154	      x ⁻¹ ∙ y                 ∎
155	```
156	
157	#### Decidability
158	
159	The coset relation is decidable exactly when membership in `H`{.AgdaBound} is:
160	whether `x ∼ y` is, definitionally, whether the single product `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` lies in
161	`H`{.AgdaBound}.[^1]
162	
163	```agda
164	  -- With decidable membership in H, the coset relation is decidable.
165	  ∼-dec : (∀ x → Dec (x ∈ H)) → ∀ x y → Dec (x ∼ y)
166	  ∼-dec H-dec x y = H-dec (x ⁻¹ ∙ y)
167	```
168	
169	#### The quotient setoid `G/H`
170	
171	The coset space is the carrier of `𝒢` under the coset equality, assembled by the
172	quotient construction of [Setoid.Relations.Quotients][].
173	
174	```agda
175	  cosetSetoid : Setoid α ℓ
176	  cosetSetoid = G / ∼-equivalence
177	```
178

20	This module proves `_∼_` is an equivalence relation and packages the quotient
21	setoid, `cosetSetoid`{.AgdaFunction}, via the `_/_`{.AgdaFunction} construction of
22	[Setoid.Relations.Quotients][].
23	
24	Two further lemmas prepare the ground for the coset action of
25	[Classical.Structures.Group.GSet][]: the original setoid equality refines the
26	coset equality (`≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction}, well-definedness of the quotient map), and
27	left translation by any group element preserves the coset equality
28	(`∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, which will be the congruence proof of the action).
29	
30	<!--
31	```agda
32	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
33	
34	module Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets where
35	
36	open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )
37	
38	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------
39	open import Data.Product     using ( _,_ ; proj₁ )
40	open import Level            using ( Level )
41	open import Relation.Binary  using ( Setoid ; IsEquivalence )
42	open import Relation.Nullary using ( Dec )
43	open import Relation.Unary   using ( Pred ; _∈_ )
44	
45	import Algebra.Properties.Group as GroupProperties
46	import Relation.Binary.Reasoning.Setoid as SetoidReasoning
47	
48	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------
49	open import Overture                              using ( Equivalence )
50	open import Classical.Bundles.Group               using ( ⟨_⟩ᵍᵖ )
51	open import Classical.Structures.Group.Basic      using ( Group ; module Group-Op )
52	open import Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups  using ( IsSubgroup )
53	open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic                 using ( Algebra ; 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] )
54	open import Setoid.Relations.Quotients            using ( _/_ )
55	```
56	-->
57	
58	#### The coset relation
59	
60	```agda
61	module Coset {α ρ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) {ℓ : Level}
62	  (H : Pred 𝕌[ proj₁ 𝒢 ] ℓ) (H-isSubgroup : IsSubgroup 𝒢 H)
63	  where
64	
65	  private
66	    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
67	    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
68	
69	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]            using ( _≈_ )
70	                                renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
71	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
72	  open Group-Op 𝒢               using  ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
73	                                       ; assoc-law ; invˡ-law )
74	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ  using  ( ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙
75	                                       ; \\-leftDividesˡ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
76	  open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup  using  ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed ; ⁻¹-closed )
77	
78	  infix 4 _∼_
79	
80	  -- x and y lie in the same left coset of H when x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H.
81	  _∼_ : G → G → Type ℓ
82	  x ∼ y = x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H
83	```
84	
85	#### `_∼_` is an equivalence relation
86	
87	+  Reflexivity is `ε ∈ H` transported along `x ⁻¹ ∙ x ≈ ε`.
88	+  Symmetry is closure of `H` under inverses, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x`.
89	+  Transitivity is closure under products, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z`.
90	
91	```agda
92	  ∼-refl : ∀ {x} → x ∼ x
93	  ∼-refl {x} = respects (≈sym (invˡ-law x)) ε-closed
94	
95	  ∼-sym : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → y ∼ x
96	  ∼-sym {x} {y} x∼y = respects inv-eq (⁻¹-closed x∼y)
97	    where
98	    inv-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x
99	    inv-eq = begin
100	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (x ⁻¹) y ⟩
101	      y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-involutive x) ⟩
102	      y ⁻¹ ∙ x          ∎
103	
104	  ∼-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x ∼ y → y ∼ z → x ∼ z
105	  ∼-trans {x} {y} {z} x∼y y∼z = respects prod-eq (∙-closed x∼y y∼z)
106	    where
107	    prod-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z
108	    prod-eq = begin
109	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z)  ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) y (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ⟩
110	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (y ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesˡ y z) ⟩
111	      x ⁻¹ ∙ z                 ∎
112	
113	  ∼-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _∼_
114	  ∼-isEquivalence = record { refl = ∼-refl ; sym = ∼-sym ; trans = ∼-trans }
115	
116	  ∼-equivalence : Equivalence G {ℓ}
117	  ∼-equivalence = _∼_ , ∼-isEquivalence
118	```
119	
120	#### Compatibility lemmas
121	
122	Two facts are needed before the coset relation can be used as an equality.
123	
124	`≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} says the group's own setoid equality refines the coset
125	relation, which is what makes the quotient map well defined: equal elements land
126	in the same coset.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} says left translation by any group
127	element preserves the coset relation, which is what lets `g ∙_` descend to the
128	coset space.
129	
130	Both are proved the same way, by supplying `respects`{.AgdaFunction} with an
131	equality between the relevant `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` witnesses: for `≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} that
132	witness reduces to `ε` and membership follows from `ε-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, and for
133	`∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} the `g` cancels, so the translated witness equals the
134	original.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} is what
135	[Classical.Structures.Group.GSet][] uses to build the coset algebra.
136	
137	```agda
138	  -- The setoid equality refines the coset equality (the quotient map is well defined).
139	  ≈⇒∼ : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∼ y
140	  ≈⇒∼ {x} {y} x≈y = respects (≈sym unit-eq) ε-closed
141	    where
142	    unit-eq : x ⁻¹ ∙ y ≈ ε
143	    unit-eq = ≈trans (∙-cong (⁻¹-cong x≈y) ≈refl) (invˡ-law y)
144	
145	  -- Left translation by any group element preserves the coset equality.
146	  ∼-congˡ : ∀ g {x y} → x ∼ y → (g ∙ x) ∼ (g ∙ y)
147	  ∼-congˡ g {x} {y} x∼y = respects (≈sym transl-eq) x∼y
148	    where
149	    transl-eq : (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ y
150	    transl-eq = begin
151	      (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)     ≈⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ≈refl ⟩
152	      x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)    ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) (g ∙ y) ⟩
153	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g y) ⟩
154	      x ⁻¹ ∙ y                 ∎
155	```
156	
157	#### Decidability
158	
159	The coset relation is decidable exactly when membership in `H`{.AgdaBound} is:
160	whether `x ∼ y` is, definitionally, whether the single product `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` lies in
161	`H`{.AgdaBound}.[^1]
162	
163	```agda
164	  -- With decidable membership in H, the coset relation is decidable.
165	  ∼-dec : (∀ x → Dec (x ∈ H)) → ∀ x y → Dec (x ∼ y)
166	  ∼-dec H-dec x y = H-dec (x ⁻¹ ∙ y)
167	```
168	
169	#### The quotient setoid `G/H`
170	
171	The coset space is the carrier of `𝒢` under the coset equality, assembled by the
172	quotient construction of [Setoid.Relations.Quotients][].
173	
174	```agda
175	  cosetSetoid : Setoid α ℓ
176	  cosetSetoid = G / ∼-equivalence
177	```
178	
179	---
180	
181	[^1]:  This is the Layer-D decision procedure that sits beside the semantic
182	       relation, per the two-layer discipline ([ADR-008]; audit A2 of
183	       `docs/notes/flrp-wp7-audits.md`).

9	### Groups {#classical-structures-group}
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	A **group** is an inhabitant of the `Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ Th-Group` type,
14	where `Algebra` is parameterized by the signature type `Sig-Group`.
15	
16	The signature of `Group` grows over its predecessor's by a *unary* symbol
17	(`Sig-Group` adds `⁻¹-Op` to `Sig-Monoid`); its forgetful projection
18	`group→monoid` is therefore a reduct that drops `⁻¹-Op`, discharging the three
19	monoid equations on the reduct by the curried-law pivot of the `monoid→semigroup`
20	of [`Classical.Structures.Monoid`][Classical.Structures.Monoid] (here extended
21	from one law to three, the two identity laws additionally bridging the nullary
22	`ε-Op` node).
23	
24	This module follows the [Monoid][Classical.Structures.Monoid] template, adding the
25	following to it.
26	
27	+  **Direct curried accessors for all three operations**.
28	   `Group-Op` defines `_∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑨)`, `ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑨)`, and
29	   `_⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨)` directly over `Sig-Group`, never inheriting through
30	   the reduct, for the same reason Monoid gives: keeping the accessors direct
31	   keeps every downstream `refl` off the reduct's position-map reduction.
32	
33	+  **A unary node-bridge**.  Alongside the binary `interp-node-∙` and nullary
34	   `interp-node-ε`, `Group-Op` has `interp-node-⁻¹` for the unary `⁻¹-Op`, a
35	   one-liner delegating to `interp-cong` exactly as the other two do.
36	
37	+  **Two inverse laws**.  `invˡ-law` and `invʳ-law` join the three monoid laws in
38	   `Group-Op`; they are the only laws not consumed by the forgetful projection
39	   (which lands in `Monoid`, below the inverse structure), so they live in
40	   `Group-Op` rather than in the standalone curried-law block.
41	
42	<!--

87	-->
88	
89	#### The local satisfaction predicate
90	
91	```agda
92	infix 4 _⊨ᵍᵖ_
93	_⊨ᵍᵖ_ :  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ)
94	        (ℰ : Eq-Group → Term (Fin 3) × Term (Fin 3)) → Type (α ⊔ ρ)
95	𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ ℰ = ∀ i → 𝑨 ⊧ proj₁ (ℰ i) ≈ proj₂ (ℰ i)
96	```
97	
98	#### The type of groups
99	
100	`Group`{.AgdaFunction}` α ρ` pairs an algebra over `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} with a
101	proof of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction}.  Its own signature since the identity is a nullary
102	operation and the inverse is a unary one, and neither can be added to a weaker
103	signature by equations alone.  The five equations of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction} are
104	associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws.
105	
106	```agda
107	Group : (α ρ : Level) → Type (suc α ⊔ suc ρ)
108	Group α ρ = Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
109	```
110	
111	#### The reduct to monoids
112	
113	The container morphism `Sig-Monoid ⟹ Sig-Group` sends the monoid's `∙-Opᵐᵒ` and
114	`ε-Opᵐᵒ` to the group's `∙-Op` and `ε-Op`; the position maps are the identity.
115	`group→monoidAlg` is the induced reduct of the underlying algebra.
116	
117	```agda
118	mo-incl : Op-Monoid → Op-Group
119	mo-incl ∙-Opᵐᵒ = ∙-Op
120	mo-incl ε-Opᵐᵒ = ε-Op
121	
122	mo-κ : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Monoid)
123	  → ArityOf Sig-Group (mo-incl o) → ArityOf Sig-Monoid o
124	mo-κ ∙-Opᵐᵒ = id
125	mo-κ ε-Opᵐᵒ = id
126	
127	group→monoidAlg : Group α ρ → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} α ρ
128	group→monoidAlg 𝑮 = reductBy mo-incl mo-κ (𝑮 .proj₁)
129	```
130	
131	#### Curried associativity, standalone
132	
133	`gp-assoc` proves `x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)` for the group's own `∙`, a verbatim
134	port of `Monoid-Op.mn-assoc` to `Sig-Group`.  It is standalone, above the
135	forgetful projection, so both `Group-Op.assoc-law` and `group→monoid` consume one
136	proof.
137	
138	```agda
139	module _ ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
140	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl)
141	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
142	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
143	
144	  private
145	    infixl 7 _∙_
146	    _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
147	    _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
148	
149	    interp-node∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
150	      → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
151	    interp-node∙ s t η = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
152	
153	  gp-assoc : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
154	  gp-assoc x y z = begin
155	    x ∙ y ∙ z                ≈˘⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ ⟩
156	    ⟦ node ∙-Op lhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations assoc η ⟩
157	    ⟦ node ∙-Op rhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ' ⟩
158	    x ∙ (y ∙ z)              ∎
159	    where
160	    g0 g1 g2 : Term (Fin 3)
161	    g0 = ℊ 0F; g1 = ℊ 1F; g2 = ℊ 2F
162	
163	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
164	    η = λ { 0F → x ; 1F → y ; 2F → z }
165	
166	    lhs rhs : Fin 2 → Term (Fin 3)
167	    lhs = pair (node ∙-Op (pair g0 g1)) g2
168	    rhs = pair g0 (node ∙-Op (pair g1 g2))
169	
170	    γ : ∀ i → ⟦ lhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair (x ∙ y) z i
171	    γ = λ { 0F → interp-node∙ g0 g1 η; 1F → ≈refl }
172	
173	    γ' : ∀ i → ⟦ rhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair x (y ∙ z) i
174	    γ' = λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → interp-node∙ g1 g2 η }
175	```
176	
177	#### The `Group-Op` module
178	
179	`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}` 𝑮` is the named-accessor module for a fixed group, opened
180	at a use site so that the laws read in ordinary notation.  It rebuilds the
181	interface from `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} directly rather than inheriting it,
182	because the forgetful to monoids is a reduct along a signature morphism and so
183	carries nothing down.
184	
185	The three operations come first, curried out of their interpretations:
186	`_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε`{.AgdaFunction} and `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}.
187	`equations`{.AgdaFunction} is the satisfaction witness projected out of the Σ.
188	Then come the two congruences, `∙-cong`{.AgdaFunction} and
189	`⁻¹-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, and the three containment lemmas
190	`interp-node-∙`{.AgdaFunction}, `interp-node-ε`{.AgdaFunction} and
191	`interp-node-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}, one per operation symbol, each crossing the gap
192	between a law stated about interpreted terms and the same law in curried form.
193	
194	The five laws follow: `assoc-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `idˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction},
195	`idʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `invˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction} and `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.
196	Each is its `equations` step wrapped in the containment lemmas for the symbols it
197	mentions, so the inverse laws are the longest of the five: they mention all three
198	operations.
199	
200	```agda
201	module Group-Op {α ρ : Level} ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
202	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (trans to ≈trans; sym to ≈sym; refl to ≈refl)
203	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
204	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
205	
206	  infixl 7 _∙_
207	  _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
208	  _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
209	
210	  ε : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
211	  ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑮)
212	
213	  infix 8 _⁻¹
214	  _⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
215	  _⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑮)
216	
217	  ∙-cong : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x ∙ u ≈ y ∙ v
218	  ∙-cong x≈y u≈v = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → x≈y ; 1F → u≈v }
219	
220	  ⁻¹-cong : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹
221	  ⁻¹-cong x≈y = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → x≈y }
222	
223	  interp-node-∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
224	    → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
225	  interp-node-∙ s t = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
226	
227	  interp-node-ε : {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]} → ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
228	  interp-node-ε = interp-cong 𝑮 ε-Op (λ ())
229	
230	  interp-node-⁻¹ : (s : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
231	    → ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → s) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ⁻¹
232	  interp-node-⁻¹ s = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl }
233	
234	  assoc-law : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
235	  assoc-law = gp-assoc (𝑮 , equations)
236	
237	  idˡ-law : ∀ x → ε ∙ x ≈ x
238	  idˡ-law x = begin
239	    ε ∙ x                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong interp-node-ε ≈refl ⟩
240	    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0 ⟩

14	where `Algebra` is parameterized by the signature type `Sig-Group`.
15	
16	The signature of `Group` grows over its predecessor's by a *unary* symbol
17	(`Sig-Group` adds `⁻¹-Op` to `Sig-Monoid`); its forgetful projection
18	`group→monoid` is therefore a reduct that drops `⁻¹-Op`, discharging the three
19	monoid equations on the reduct by the curried-law pivot of the `monoid→semigroup`
20	of [`Classical.Structures.Monoid`][Classical.Structures.Monoid] (here extended
21	from one law to three, the two identity laws additionally bridging the nullary
22	`ε-Op` node).
23	
24	This module follows the [Monoid][Classical.Structures.Monoid] template, adding the
25	following to it.
26	
27	+  **Direct curried accessors for all three operations**.
28	   `Group-Op` defines `_∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑨)`, `ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑨)`, and
29	   `_⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨)` directly over `Sig-Group`, never inheriting through
30	   the reduct, for the same reason Monoid gives: keeping the accessors direct
31	   keeps every downstream `refl` off the reduct's position-map reduction.
32	
33	+  **A unary node-bridge**.  Alongside the binary `interp-node-∙` and nullary
34	   `interp-node-ε`, `Group-Op` has `interp-node-⁻¹` for the unary `⁻¹-Op`, a
35	   one-liner delegating to `interp-cong` exactly as the other two do.
36	
37	+  **Two inverse laws**.  `invˡ-law` and `invʳ-law` join the three monoid laws in
38	   `Group-Op`; they are the only laws not consumed by the forgetful projection
39	   (which lands in `Monoid`, below the inverse structure), so they live in
40	   `Group-Op` rather than in the standalone curried-law block.

88	
89	#### The local satisfaction predicate
90	
91	```agda
92	infix 4 _⊨ᵍᵖ_
93	_⊨ᵍᵖ_ :  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ)
94	        (ℰ : Eq-Group → Term (Fin 3) × Term (Fin 3)) → Type (α ⊔ ρ)
95	𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ ℰ = ∀ i → 𝑨 ⊧ proj₁ (ℰ i) ≈ proj₂ (ℰ i)
96	```
97	
98	#### The type of groups
99	
100	`Group`{.AgdaFunction}` α ρ` pairs an algebra over `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} with a
101	proof of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction}.  Its own signature since the identity is a nullary
102	operation and the inverse is a unary one, and neither can be added to a weaker
103	signature by equations alone.  The five equations of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction} are
104	associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws.
105	
106	```agda
107	Group : (α ρ : Level) → Type (suc α ⊔ suc ρ)
108	Group α ρ = Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
109	```
110	
111	#### The reduct to monoids
112	
113	The container morphism `Sig-Monoid ⟹ Sig-Group` sends the monoid's `∙-Opᵐᵒ` and
114	`ε-Opᵐᵒ` to the group's `∙-Op` and `ε-Op`; the position maps are the identity.
115	`group→monoidAlg` is the induced reduct of the underlying algebra.
116	
117	```agda
118	mo-incl : Op-Monoid → Op-Group
119	mo-incl ∙-Opᵐᵒ = ∙-Op
120	mo-incl ε-Opᵐᵒ = ε-Op
121	
122	mo-κ : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Monoid)
123	  → ArityOf Sig-Group (mo-incl o) → ArityOf Sig-Monoid o
124	mo-κ ∙-Opᵐᵒ = id
125	mo-κ ε-Opᵐᵒ = id
126	
127	group→monoidAlg : Group α ρ → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} α ρ
128	group→monoidAlg 𝑮 = reductBy mo-incl mo-κ (𝑮 .proj₁)
129	```
130	
131	#### Curried associativity, standalone
132	
133	`gp-assoc` proves `x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)` for the group's own `∙`, a verbatim
134	port of `Monoid-Op.mn-assoc` to `Sig-Group`.  It is standalone, above the
135	forgetful projection, so both `Group-Op.assoc-law` and `group→monoid` consume one
136	proof.

138	```agda
139	module _ ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
140	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl)
141	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
142	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
143	
144	  private
145	    infixl 7 _∙_
146	    _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
147	    _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
148	
149	    interp-node∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
150	      → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
151	    interp-node∙ s t η = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
152	
153	  gp-assoc : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
154	  gp-assoc x y z = begin
155	    x ∙ y ∙ z                ≈˘⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ ⟩
156	    ⟦ node ∙-Op lhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations assoc η ⟩
157	    ⟦ node ∙-Op rhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ' ⟩
158	    x ∙ (y ∙ z)              ∎
159	    where
160	    g0 g1 g2 : Term (Fin 3)
161	    g0 = ℊ 0F; g1 = ℊ 1F; g2 = ℊ 2F
162	
163	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
164	    η = λ { 0F → x ; 1F → y ; 2F → z }
165	
166	    lhs rhs : Fin 2 → Term (Fin 3)
167	    lhs = pair (node ∙-Op (pair g0 g1)) g2
168	    rhs = pair g0 (node ∙-Op (pair g1 g2))
169	
170	    γ : ∀ i → ⟦ lhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair (x ∙ y) z i
171	    γ = λ { 0F → interp-node∙ g0 g1 η; 1F → ≈refl }
172	
173	    γ' : ∀ i → ⟦ rhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair x (y ∙ z) i
174	    γ' = λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → interp-node∙ g1 g2 η }
175	```
176	
177	#### The `Group-Op` module
178	
179	`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}` 𝑮` is the named-accessor module for a fixed group, opened
180	at a use site so that the laws read in ordinary notation.  It rebuilds the
181	interface from `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} directly rather than inheriting it,
182	because the forgetful to monoids is a reduct along a signature morphism and so
183	carries nothing down.
184	
185	The three operations come first, curried out of their interpretations:
186	`_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε`{.AgdaFunction} and `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}.
187	`equations`{.AgdaFunction} is the satisfaction witness projected out of the Σ.
188	Then come the two congruences, `∙-cong`{.AgdaFunction} and
189	`⁻¹-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, and the three containment lemmas
190	`interp-node-∙`{.AgdaFunction}, `interp-node-ε`{.AgdaFunction} and
191	`interp-node-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}, one per operation symbol, each crossing the gap
192	between a law stated about interpreted terms and the same law in curried form.
193	
194	The five laws follow: `assoc-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `idˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction},
195	`idʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `invˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction} and `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.
196	Each is its `equations` step wrapped in the containment lemmas for the symbols it
197	mentions, so the inverse laws are the longest of the five: they mention all three
198	operations.

200	```agda
201	module Group-Op {α ρ : Level} ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
202	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (trans to ≈trans; sym to ≈sym; refl to ≈refl)
203	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
204	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
205	
206	  infixl 7 _∙_
207	  _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
208	  _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
209	
210	  ε : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
211	  ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑮)
212	
213	  infix 8 _⁻¹
214	  _⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
215	  _⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑮)
216	
217	  ∙-cong : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x ∙ u ≈ y ∙ v
218	  ∙-cong x≈y u≈v = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → x≈y ; 1F → u≈v }
219	
220	  ⁻¹-cong : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹
221	  ⁻¹-cong x≈y = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → x≈y }
222	
223	  interp-node-∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
224	    → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
225	  interp-node-∙ s t = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
226	
227	  interp-node-ε : {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]} → ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
228	  interp-node-ε = interp-cong 𝑮 ε-Op (λ ())
229	
230	  interp-node-⁻¹ : (s : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
231	    → ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → s) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ⁻¹
232	  interp-node-⁻¹ s = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl }
233	
234	  assoc-law : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
235	  assoc-law = gp-assoc (𝑮 , equations)
236	
237	  idˡ-law : ∀ x → ε ∙ x ≈ x
238	  idˡ-law x = begin
239	    ε ∙ x                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong interp-node-ε ≈refl ⟩
240	    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0 ⟩
